rule: A flag is an irregularity between a published value and the official page it cites. Severity: red = a published value is contradicted or cannot be confirmed; amber = confirmed but the evidence has a stated limit; green = checked and clean. Nothing here blocks the build; everything here is published so it can be checked.

flags.finding: No injury-report read in this repository retains raw response bytes. nfl.com cannot be reached over TLS from the sandbox's bash (curl exit 35, urllib SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL), so all three dated reads (2026-11-14, and two on 2026-11-15) are transcriptions made through a text-extraction tool.
flags.effect: A transcription cannot prove that no cell was dropped or altered during extraction. Every injury cell is 'transcribed', never 'byte-verified'. This is the single largest limit on the whole availability layer.
flags.verify: Re-fetch https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg10 and compare with data/official/2026_w10_capture_2026-11-15T1814z/official_injuries_week10_2026-11-15T1814z.psv (347 rows, SHA-256 in data/console/week10_reconcile.json).

flags.finding: The published 2026-11-14 table is missing two rows that the page prints today: Baltimore DT Calais Campbell and T Ronnie Stanley, both 'Did Not Participate In Practice' with no game designation.
flags.effect: Two Ravens cannot be joined to a depth slot, so any replacement behind them is invisible. Baltimore already has the thinnest published coverage of any club (8 of 10 printed rows).
flags.verify: Open the injury report, find the Monday LAC@BAL block, count the Ravens table: it prints 10 rows; the published table holds 8.

flags.finding: 32 cells across 16 players differ between the published 2026-11-14 table and the page as read on 2026-11-15. The designation totals moved from 66 Out / 84 Questionable / 10 Doubtful / 185 blank to 70 / 90 / 11 / 176.
flags.effect: Either the report changed between the two dates (expected: it is a daily document) or the 11-14 read carries transcription errors. The repository holds no evidence that separates the two, so no cell is 'corrected'.
flags.verify: data/console/week10_reconcile.csv lists every differing cell with both values.

flags.finding: The published Packers depth store holds 59 rows and every one stores the player name with the jersey number inside the string ('75 Sean Rhyan'). The live chart (footprint 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026') prints 55 named cells, one of which the store never captured (Kaleb Johnson, RB, 4th string) and three the live chart no longer prints (Coleman Owen at WR, KR and PR).
flags.effect: A name join against the injury report returns 0 of 17 Green Bay rows before stripping and 14 of 17 after. The Store is also incomplete, so stripping alone does not fix it.
flags.verify: Open https://www.packers.com/team/depth-chart and compare with data/console/depth_parse.csv (33 differing cells, each labelled by kind).

flags.finding: The Houston Texans serve their depth chart as a single image (static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/texans/a5or0zowuo36y1txf4ly) with no table, no list and no alt text. The repository publishes 0 of 897 depth slots for Houston.
flags.effect: Houston is a coverage hole, not a clean bill of health. A Houston starter ruled out cannot be matched to a replacement string, and the deficiency register is silent on one of 32 clubs.
flags.verify: Fetch https://www.houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart and search the served page for a table element or an img alt attribute: neither exists.

flags.finding: Every club chart in this repository is a club self-report marked 'Unofficial' by the club that publishes it. Green Bay prints the date it means ('Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'); the repository records the fetch date instead.
flags.effect: A depth row cannot be treated as a league fact, and a row fetched on the 14th that prints 'Nov. 10' is three days older than it looks.
flags.verify: The footer of https://www.packers.com/team/depth-chart and the same convention on the other 30 club pages.

flags.finding: The brief's depth item says '149 club/unit/position slots list more than one rank-1 player'. The repository's own depth store contains 893 rank-1 slots and none with more than one player at depth 1: the parser flattens each printed cell into one row keyed by (club, unit, position, slot, depth).
flags.effect: The defect the brief describes may well be real on the club pages, but this repository cannot show it, because its schema cannot represent it. The number 149 could not be reproduced and is not published as fact.
flags.verify: Count depth-1 rows per (team, unit, position, slot) in data/pipeline/depth_charts.json: 893 slots, 0 shared. Then read two club pages: Seattle prints 'Cooper Kupp' and 'Rashid Shaheed' in one WR cell, Washington prints one DL cell empty.

flags.finding: The shared-slot and empty-slot patterns the brief describes are confirmed on the live pages: Seattle prints two players in one WR cell ('Cooper Kupp' and 'Rashid Shaheed'); Washington prints 'DL Daron Payne' followed by three empty cells, and 'LB Frankie Luvu | (empty) | Kain Medrano'.
flags.effect: Confirms the schema requirement: a slot must be able to hold several players and no player, and both must be distinguishable from a ranked list.

flags.finding: The brief says 'Baltimore still publishes Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at QB after both went on injured reserve'. The live chart shows QB Jacoby Brissett (1st), Joe Fagnano (2nd) and Kedon Slovis (3rd); Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley appear nowhere on it.
flags.effect: The claim was true of some earlier publication, or of a cached page, but it is not true of the page today. It is recorded as not reproducible rather than repeated, and the underlying failure it describes (a chart going stale against transactions) is still untested.
flags.verify: Fetch https://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/depth-chart and read the QB row.

flags.finding: The brief says 'Published counts are stale: 254 rows and 4 no-injury sections versus 279 rows and 2 sections live'. Nothing in the repository holds 254 or 279 injury rows: the published table holds 345 and the page prints 347 today.
flags.effect: The specific numbers describe a different artefact (or a different page) than the one published here. The instruction behind them — re-capture and republish beside the old read — is executed in full on the re-capture page.
flags.verify: wc -l data/nfl/injuries_week10.tsv (345 data rows) and the live page's own per-club tables (28 clubs, 347 rows).

flags.finding: The brief says 'Turn the 136-game log into the pre-registered backtest corpus'. The results feed holds 272 scheduled 2026 games, of which 137 are settled. No 136-game artefact exists.
flags.effect: The correct corpus is stated from the feed rather than from the brief: 137 settled games as of 2026-11-15. The count moves every week, which is exactly why it must be frozen and hashed before a window opens.
flags.verify: Count settled rows for season 2026 in data/console/results_feed.csv.

flags.finding: The results feed has no score for the two 2026 Week 10 games that the league has since finalised: New England 10 at Detroit 35 (Sunday 15 November) and Washington 24 at NY Giants 21 (Thursday 12 November).
flags.effect: Any backtest that claims to cover 'all settled games' is two games short, and the genesis of a new score row is unverified against the league page. No score is inserted here without the game page being read.
flags.verify: https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-10 prints both finals; https://www.nfl.com/games/patriots-at-lions-2026-reg-10 is the game centre.

flags.finding: Requirement R-02 (opening and closing numbers for every originated market) is met for 1,072 of 18,902 markets, all in 2021. No source available here publishes a book, a timestamp, or an opening number for any other season.
flags.effect: Every requirement that needs a market number — residual, CLV, vig-free consensus, multi-book comparison — is blocked at the source, not at the code.
flags.verify: data/console/price_snapshots.csv: count rows with both open_line and close_line non-blank.

flags.finding: Three Green Bay players on the official injury report appear nowhere on the club's depth chart: Chris Brooks (RB), Micah Parsons (LB) and Skyy Moore (WR).
flags.effect: The source does not say whether they are on reserve, on the practice squad, or simply omitted from an unofficial chart. No reason is recorded, so each of the three is unpriced by the availability model.

flags.finding: The repository publishes four separate reads of the same Week 10 injury page in four formats (data/nfl/injuries_week10.tsv, data/verify/official_injuries_2026_w10.psv, data/console/injuries_week10.csv, data/capture/2026_w10/*.psv) plus this session's, with no single register naming which is canonical.
flags.effect: A reader cannot tell which file a published cell came from without tracing the builders. The console table and the published TSV are consistent (0 differing of 345), which is the only reason this is amber rather than red.
flags.verify: tools/official/week10_reconcile.py compares all four and reports 0 differences between the console table and the published TSV.

flags.finding: A club's live chart can contradict the league's own injury report on the same day: Green Bay lists 'Aaron Banks' as Limited in practice with no game designation, while the chart prints him as the starting left guard; Baltimore's chart lists Jaylinn Hawkins as a starting safety while the report designates him Out.
flags.effect: Two official sources disagree about who starts. Neither is wrong: the chart is 'unofficial' and dated, the report is a practice-designation document. Any starter definition must state which source it trusts.
flags.verify: Compare the Ravens' SS row on https://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/depth-chart with the 'Jaylinn Hawkins ... Out' row on the injury report.
